title: Fully Automated Centrifugal Microfluidic Device for Ultrasensitive Protein Detection from Whole Blood
protocol: Dissolve 1.5 g of titanium tetraisopropoxide in a mixture of ethanol and glacial acetic acid.
Mix the solution at room temperature for 30 min on a magnetic stirrer.
Dissolve 11 wt% of polyvinyl pyrrolidone in ethanol.
Stir the PVP solution at 65 °C for 1 hr using a hot-plate magnetic stirrer.
Combine and stir the two solutions at 65 °C for 4 hr on a hot-plate magnetic stirrer.
Load the prepared solution into a syringe connected to a stainless steel needle of 200 μm inner diameter.
Introduce the solution constantly at a flow rate of 0.3 ml/hr onto a Si wafer placed on a grounded substrate under high DC voltage (15 kV).
Set the distance between the needle and the grounded substrate to 10 cm during electrospinning.
Place the NF mat in a furnace.
Increase the temperature up to 500 °C with a ramping rate of 3 °C/min under high-vacuum condition.
Maintain the temperature at 500 °C for 3 hr.
Cool down the samples to room temperature in the furnace.
Use the 3D designing software to depict chambers, channels, or valves of each layer of disc.
Convert the design files to CNC code using code generating software.
Open the operating software of CNC milling machine and load CNC code.
Attach the PC plate on the CNC milling machine: use 1 mm PC plates for the top layer and 5 mm PC plates for the disc layer.
Run the CNC milling machine to cut each layer of the disc by clicking the "START" button.
Place a silicon substrate and a small petri dish containing 40 µL of (tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl)-1-trichlorosilane in a vacuum chamber under vacuum for 30 min.
Mix polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) pre-polymer with a curing agent in a 10:1 ratio and degas in a vacuum chamber.
Spin-coat the PDMS onto a silicon substrate at 650 rpm for 60 sec.
Cure the PDMS coated on silicon substrate in an oven at 65 °C for 10 min to achieve an adherent state.
Transfer the TiO2 NF mat prepared by electrospinning and calcination onto the PDMS-coated silicon using a tweezer.
Manually apply conformal pressure on the transferred TiO2 NF mat with a flat object (e.g., glass slide) and remove the object.
Put this sample in the oven at 65 °C for 4 hr or at 80 °C for 1 hr to cure the PDMS layer completely.
Coat binding reaction chambers in the disc with 20 µl of the PDMS/curing agent mixture (10:1).
Dispense 50 µl of ethanol (99.9%) on the TiO2 NF mat on the PDMS layer.
Cut the TiO2 NF mat with a punch hole of 6 mm diameter and transfer to the binding reaction chambers coated with PDMS in the previous step.
Incubate the TiO2 NF mat integrated disc in the oven at 65 °C for 4 hr or at 80 °C for 1 hr to cure the PDMS completely.
Prepare a 1% v/v solution of (3-glycidoxypropyl)methyldiethoxy silane (GPDES) in ethanol (99.9%).
Treat the TiO2 NF mat integrated disc with oxygen plasma at 140 W and 50 sccm oxygen flow for 180 seconds.
Dispense 100 μl of GPDES solution on each nanofiber mat.
Incubate the substrates at room temperature (25 °C) for 2 hours.
Wash the substrates briefly with ethanol (99.9%) using a wash bottle.
Remove the ethanol completely by inverting the disc and blotting it against a clean wipe.
Cure the substrates at 80 °C for 1 hour.
Wash the substrates twice with ethanol (99.9%) in the same manner as previously stated to remove unbound GPDES molecules.
Blow dry the substrates with a nitrogen stream.
Dry the substrates under vacuum.
Make a solution of 200 μg/ml capture antibodies by diluting the antibodies with PBS buffer (pH 7.4).
Dispense 5 μl of antibody solution onto each NF mat in a disc using a micropipette.
Incubate the discs in a humidified chamber at 37 °C for 4 hours.
Wash the antibodies coated NF mat with 0.1% BSA-PBS buffer.
Fill the chamber with 100 μl of wash buffer using a micropipette.
Remove the buffer by aspirating or decanting.
Invert the disc and blot it against a clean wipe.
Assemble the disc.
Draw the design of the disc on double-side adhesive tape using a CAD program.
Load the CAD design to the cutting plotter.
Cut the double-side adhesive tape using the cutting plotter.
Peel off one protection layer of double adhesive tape and attach it on top of the disc layer.
Peel off the other protection layer and attach the top layer on the disc layer.
Load the preliminarily assembled disc in the pressing machine.
Precisely align top/adhesive/disc layers using align marks in each layer to connect each valve, channel, and chambers.
Apply conformal pressure using the pressing machine.
Fill the chambers with 1% BSA-PBS buffer using a micropipette.
Incubate the disc at 37 °C for 1 hr.
Remove the buffer by aspiration using a micropipette.
Wash twice with 0.1% BSA-PBS by filling and aspirating the chambers using a micropipette.
Spin the disc at 3,600 rpm (391 x g) for 60 seconds to separate the red blood cells.
Open valve #1 by laser irradiation.
Transfer 4 μl of the supernatant plasma to the chamber containing 8 μl of detecting antibodies conjugated with HRP by spinning the disc at 2,400 rpm for 3 seconds.
Apply a mixing mode (15 Hz s-1, 15°) for 5 seconds for binding of the protein and detection antibodies.
Open valve #2.
Transfer the mixture to the binding reaction chamber (2,400 rpm, 3 seconds).
Apply a mixing mode (60 Hz s-1, 2°) for 20 minutes to achieve an immunoreaction between the mixture and the binding antibodies on the TiO2 NFs.
Open valve #3 after the reaction.
Transfer the residual mixture to the waste chamber (2,400 rpm, 10 seconds).
Transfer 600 μl of washing buffer to the binding reaction chamber by opening valve #4 and spinning the disc at 2,400 rpm for 4 seconds.
Apply a mixing mode (30 Hz s-1, 30°) for 120 seconds to wash the TiO2 NFs in the chamber.
Wash the TiO2 NFs twice more by following the same conditions as step 3.8.
Remove the residual washing buffer completely by spinning the disc at 2,400 rpm for 20 seconds.
Close valve #5.
Mix the chemiluminescent substrate solution with a mixing mode (30 Hz s-1, 2°) for 1 min after transferring it to the binding reaction chamber.
Spin the disc at 2,400 rpm for 10 sec after opening valve #6.
Transfer the reacted substrate solution to the detection chambers by opening valve #7 and spinning the disc at 2,400 rpm for 10 sec.
Measure chemiluminescence signals from the reacted substrate solution using a photomultiplier tube (PMT) module equipped detection system.
